text: Discharge instructions for a 72-year-old man admitted with acute on chronic HFrEF, EF 30%, community-acquired right lower lobe pneumonia, and acute kidney injury, improved. New medications: Furosemide 40 mg by mouth once daily for volume management. Losartan 25 mg by mouth once daily for heart failure and blood pressure control. Empagliflozin 10 mg by mouth once daily for heart failure and diabetes. Amoxicillin-clavulanate 875/125 mg by mouth twice daily for 3 additional days to complete treatment for pneumonia. Continue Metoprolol succinate 50 mg once daily, Apixaban 5 mg twice daily, Atorvastatin 40 mg nightly, and Metformin 500 mg twice daily provided renal function remains stable. Stopped: Lisinopril, discontinued because therapy was changed to losartan. Held: Spironolactone, pending repeat renal function and potassium. Avoid ibuprofen and other NSAIDs. Instructions: low-sodium diet, about 2 grams of sodium daily. Monitor daily weight each morning and keep a written record. Complete the entire antibiotic course. Obtain a basic metabolic panel at the early follow-up. Follow up with primary care and cardiology within approximately 1 week. Return precautions: seek urgent medical attention for new or worsening shortness of breath, chest pain or pressure, fainting or severe dizziness, rapidly worsening leg or abdominal swelling, significant decrease in urine output, new confusion or severe weakness, or fever or worsening cough despite antibiotics.
